title: Hooks
summary: A hook is what xtpd runs when a session for a registered service is accepted. exec: socketpair, the program gets one end as stdin and stdout, xtpd pumps the other to the session (first user: sshd -i for ssh.management). rexx: the session object goes to an ooRexx method in a hook process. fd: a connected descriptor is passed over a unix socket to a waiting local process. Hooks run as separate processes; a crashing hook ends only its own sessions.
authority: design (architecture Tom Dyer; written by Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-24)
invariants: A hook never chooses its protection, route or priority: they come from its registration
A hook process cannot take xtpd down
procedure: ssh.management registers the exec hook sshd -i; no TCP listener remains

provenance.claim: XTP sessions: one context, both directions, per-direction close, one listener socket for all sessions
